isolated_qa_evidence.scope: Parser, catalog/definer/ACL fingerprint, guard and trigger rejection probes, all twelve successful transition paths with rollback, four targeted lock/clock concurrency races, five caller-failure/timeout/disconnect probes, 28 targeted generated-key/CHECK/trigger/FK/normalization probes, 37 exact UTF-8 normalization vectors plus nine class-identity routine prechecks, and 28 direct constraint outcomes (24 reject and four accept) against all 47 source migrations on disposable PostgreSQL 15.18 en_US.utf8, plus a synthetic schema/content/catalog/privilege backup-restore match. The differential found that the PostgreSQL actor CHECK makes its nominal ON DELETE SET NULL reject a referenced user deletion; the MariaDB FK now preserves that effective outcome with RESTRICT. Error-then-COMMIT persisted earlier routine writes and is an observed activation risk. This is not exhaustive PostgreSQL differential, full concurrency/fault, adapter, activation, production recovery, or production evidence.

invariant_core.routine_owns: All invariant-bearing writes, including protected users lifecycle columns, plus matching status history
invariant_core.caller_owns: Authentication, authorization, idempotency, audit, later-phase cleanup, and cryptographic invite candidate generation in the same caller transaction
invariant_core.activation_proof: Any caller-owned failure must roll back the routine writes

full_domain.routine_owns: Every domain write, including audit, idempotency, and later-phase cleanup
full_domain.activation_proof: Cannot be implemented before all referenced manifest phases exist

runtime_credential_threat_model.option_a_boundary: Trusted application and operator adapters own the transaction and must roll back the complete caller transaction on every routine or later caller-owned failure.
runtime_credential_threat_model.authorization_boundary: Caller authentication and authorization are not database-bound. Definer routines accept actor, user, and operator ids as parameters; the two column-scoped direct UPDATE paths rely on caller WHERE/row-version CAS. Possession of a runtime credential is not proof of an authenticated product principal, row scope, or CAS predicate.
runtime_credential_threat_model.arbitrary_runtime_sql_protection: Not provided by option A: a stolen runtime credential can invoke authorized routines with chosen actor/user/operator ids, issue allowed direct UPDATEs against chosen class/member rows without the application CAS, and may commit earlier procedure substatements after an error.
runtime_credential_threat_model.required_fault_proof: Pinned MariaDB 11.4 cut-point tests cover SIGNAL, native constraint error, deadlock, lock timeout, cancellation/disconnect, and caller audit/idempotency/cleanup failure; the adapter proves zero persistence, rollback-only behavior, and safe pooled-connection reuse. Separate error-then-COMMIT probes measure the database behavior without assuming CALL statement atomicity.
runtime_credential_threat_model.measured_fault_evidence: A representative successful class-creation CALL followed by a caller-owned idempotency constraint error left zero rows with explicit ROLLBACK or client disconnect, but persisted the earlier class/member/history/invite writes when the error was ignored and COMMIT was forced. A membership lock timeout (1205) and server-side connection kill also left zero student-transition rows after disconnect. Full per-routine and adapter fault proof remains open.

fault_injection_matrix.caller_owned_failure_requirement: For each of the twelve routines, after a successful CALL and before COMMIT, separately inject every named caller-owned audit, idempotency, or cleanup failure for that transition and prove zero persistence for both routine-owned and caller-owned writes.
fault_injection_matrix.column_scoped_caller_owned_failure_requi: For each of the two column-scoped transactions, after the protected UPDATE succeeds and before COMMIT, inject the caller-owned audit failure and prove zero persistence for both the UPDATE and audit write.

fault_injection_matrix.native_and_trigger_requirement: Inject every publicly allowlisted native constraint error plus representative unknown native and status-history trigger errors after earlier writes, then prove complete caller-transaction rollback and internal fail-closed translation where not allowlisted.

runtime_credential_threat_model.if_arbitrary_runtime_sql_is_required: Reopen the ownership decision and add an unforgeable authorization-bearing database boundary for routines and both direct-DML paths plus proven error atomicity, or choose another transaction/auth ownership model before activation.

sql_deployment_packaging.target_database: The reviewed runner selects classhub_mariadb_phase1_dev explicitly; no file may rely on an ambient default database.
sql_deployment_packaging.client_contract: Use a pinned MariaDB client path that interprets DELIMITER directives exactly and does not split routine bodies with a generic semicolon parser.
sql_deployment_packaging.session_fingerprint: Before every file, prove exact server version, DATABASE(), time_zone, character_set_connection, collation_connection, sql_mode, and effective apply identity.
sql_deployment_packaging.implicit_commit_ledger: Record exact source checksum and before/after catalog state for every CREATE/GRANT/REVOKE implicit-commit boundary; never claim a multi-file transaction.

transaction_boundary.assertion_position: after the final invariant-bearing write and before commit
transaction_boundary.required_isolation: READ-COMMITTED for the complete caller transaction; all twelve routines and all three internal helpers fail closed when the caller session default is different. Effective one-shot SET TRANSACTION isolation is not observable inside a SQL SECURITY DEFINER routine without broader server visibility and remains an activation blocker.
transaction_boundary.required_isolation_probe: Pinned MariaDB 11.4 proved that @@SESSION.transaction_isolation remains the session default after one-shot SET TRANSACTION. information_schema.INNODB_TRX requires global PROCESS, while Performance Schema hides the caller thread in a fresh SQL SECURITY DEFINER call; PROCESS is forbidden for the locked owner. The adapter must initialize and reset every pooled connection with SESSION READ COMMITTED, never issue one-shot isolation overrides, and prove own-write visibility plus fresh statement snapshots. Runtime activation remains blocked until that trusted-adapter boundary is explicitly accepted or a narrower database-enforced design is approved.
transaction_boundary.existing_class_lock_order: users in numeric id order when required; then classes in numeric id order; then class_members under their locked parent class
transaction_boundary.member_cursor_order_semantics: class_members id-ascending labels describe deterministic cursor fetch order after the parent class fence; physical record-lock acquisition order is not a safety premise except where a transition names an explicit forced access-path proof
transaction_boundary.two_user_cursor_access_path: The four member-admin routines and transfer_class_teacher use FORCE INDEX (PRIMARY), numeric ORDER BY id, and FOR UPDATE for their two-user cursor. Pinned MariaDB 11.4 EXPLAIN plus reversed actor/target overlapping-session lock traces must still prove PRIMARY access and actual ascending user-row lock acquisition; source order alone is not evidence.
transaction_boundary.membership_request_exception: PRD/우리반_허브_PRD_FINAL.md:481 requires users:actor and the cross-class current-membership fence before classes:invite-target. The routine locks and rejects teacher-profile presence between that fence and the target class so source error precedence is preserved; the locked user serializes compliant user/profile/membership writers.
transaction_boundary.caller_pre_call_lock_requirement: The caller must acquire any required user locks before CALL and must not already hold a class or member lock in the opposite order; application wiring changes every caller atomically before activation
transaction_boundary.new_class_exception: create_class_with_teacher_and_invite locks actor/member/profile/school preconditions, inserts the class, then immediately locks the new classes row because no target row exists before insert
transaction_boundary.final_assertion_serialization: The locked classes row is the sole cross-table serialization fence. Dependent class_members/users/teacher_profiles/invite aggregates use fresh nonlocking READ-COMMITTED statement snapshots so the helper never takes a teacher user/profile lock after a class lock. This is safe only after every invariant writer and direct-DML denial switches atomically.
transaction_boundary.database_clock: Every routine textually captures UTC_TIMESTAMP(6) once at its reviewed transition-specific time-decision or pre-write boundary and returns it through out_occurred_at. This is not a blanket claim that capture follows every later check, reacquisition of an already-owned row, or lock on a newly inserted row; static ordering alone does not prove post-wait freshness.
transaction_boundary.database_clock_runtime_probe: On pinned MariaDB 11.4, hold the invite and class locks in session A, start request_class_membership in session B before invite expiry, release A only after expiry, and prove B rejects the expired invite. A separate nonexpired control must prove a successful request's out_occurred_at is no earlier than release of its governing invite lock. For every routine, prove capture freshness at its documented transition-specific time-decision/write boundary; do not infer stored CALL or UTC_TIMESTAMP/NOW semantics from source position or require capture to follow a later reacquisition of an already-owned row or a lock on a newly inserted row.
transaction_boundary.database_clock_runtime_evidence: Pinned MariaDB 11.4 passed both request_class_membership controls: a request begun while the invite was active rejected with 30205 after waiting across expiry, and a nonexpired success returned out_occurred_at no earlier than a database timestamp written immediately before the governing locks were released. The other eleven routines' transition-specific clock boundaries remain open.
transaction_boundary.error_contract: Any SIGNAL, constraint error, deadlock, timeout, or later caller-owned failure requires the adapter to rollback the complete caller transaction; catching a routine error and committing is forbidden

routine_interface.invite_collision_handling: Narrow 1062 handler around only the invite INSERT; inspect the last diagnostic condition, require MYSQL_ERRNO 1062 and an exact class_invite_codes_code_unique MESSAGE_TEXT suffix, RESIGNAL every mismatch, and require pinned MariaDB diagnostic and concurrency proof
routine_interface.audit_before_state: Caller captures reviewed before-state under the same ordered locks before CALL and uses routine outputs for after-state and timestamp

adapter_wire_format.datetime6: Bind the session to UTC and round-trip out_occurred_at as an exact canonical value retaining all six fractional digits; do not pass it through JavaScript Date before the caller-owned audit write. Prove byte/value equality with the routine-written history created_at.
adapter_wire_format.signed_bigint: Bind every BIGINT input/output losslessly as string or bigint, never JavaScript number. Probe values near signed BIGINT maximum and prove lossless OUT ids plus strict numeric ordering and exact decimal serialization of delete_user_account class-id JSON before CALL.

protected_transitions.lock_set_stabilization: Caller discovers affected class ids. Routine validates a bounded JSON array of positive signed BIGINT ids in strict ascending order, locks the user, locks every listed class, then current-locking-reads all memberships and requires exact distinct set equality before any write.
protected_transitions.all_history_lock_path_proof: Both user_id all-history cursors FORCE the explicit class_members_user_class_id_idx (user_id,class_id,id). Pinned MariaDB 11.4 SHOW CREATE TABLE, EXPLAIN, and concurrency traces must still prove the intended access path and class_id,id lock acquisition order.
caller_transaction_preconditions: confirmation literal equals the current API account-deletion token
caller has locked the user before discovering the expected class ids without class or member row locks
current session is valid after the user lock
current password matches the locked users.password_hash
the user is not an approved teacher of any active or suspended class
protected_transitions.required_final_assertion_scope: Assert every stabilized affected class in ascending class id order after the final invariant-bearing write and before commit

protected_transitions.cross_class_current_membership_fence: The incoming user lock is acquired before the target class; the later current-membership locking read may find another class and is safe only while all user-owned membership writers take that same user lock first. Class-wide archive never waits on a student user after member locks.
caller_preconditions: operator authentication and locked revalidation before CALL
caller_audit_requirements: always append class.teacher_transferred and teacher.transferred records in the same transaction
when the locked target was suspended, also append class.reactivated to both class and operator audit logs using the routine timestamp
routine_preconditions: incoming teacher profile is active and temporary_password_must_change is false
incoming user has no current membership
incoming user has no prior member row in the target class
a suspended target is reactivated and all suspended metadata is cleared in the same transaction
protected_transitions.known_source_divergence: The current PostgreSQL operator CLI reuses prior target-class teacher rows and omits temporary-password and suspended-class reactivation rules; MariaDB adapter wiring must replace that behavior with this PRD-authoritative contract before activation.

future_phase_activation.requirement: Before any transition activates, every entry named in caller_transaction_dependencies and future_phase_dependencies must resolve through the exact dependency artifact map, exist in the target manifest/schema, and be wired into the same caller transaction with rollback fault proof. Every entry named in post_commit_effects must have a proven after-commit dispatch path. Regenerate and re-prove the complete desired-state ACL for every then-current phase role and grant; a nonempty dependency list is not activation evidence and no partial phase parity may be claimed.
